stem: Convert 60 km/h to metres per second. Give your answer correct to 2 decimal places.
hint: Multiply by 1000 to convert km to m, then divide by 3600 to convert hours to seconds.
explanation:
To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by $\dfrac{1000}{3600} = \dfrac{1}{3.6}$.

$$60 \times \frac{1000}{3600} = \frac{60000}{3600} = 16.\overline{6} \approx 16.67 \text{ m/s}$$

stem: Train A departs at 8:30 am travelling at 110 km/h. Train B departs from the same station at 9:00 am on a parallel track, travelling at 130 km/h in the same direction. How many minutes after Train B departs will it catch Train A?
hint: Find how far ahead Train A is when Train B departs. Then divide that gap by the closing speed (difference in speeds).
explanation:
By 9:00 am, Train A has been travelling for 30 minutes = 0.5 h.

$$\text{Head start} = 110 \times 0.5 = 55 \text{ km}$$

Train B closes the gap at $130 - 110 = 20$ km/h.

$$\text{Time to close gap} = \frac{55}{20} = 2.75 \text{ h} = 2.75 \times 60 = 165 \text{ min}$$

stem: A car can travel 480 km on a full 40-litre tank of fuel. Fuel costs \$2.10 per litre. How much does it cost in fuel to drive 750 km? Give your answer to the nearest cent.
hint: First find the fuel consumption in L/100 km, then calculate the litres needed for 750 km, then multiply by the cost per litre.
explanation:
Step 1: Find fuel consumption.
$$\text{Consumption} = \frac{40}{480} \times 100 = 8.\overline{3} \text{ L/100 km}$$

Step 2: Litres needed for 750 km.
$$\text{Litres} = \frac{750}{100} \times \frac{40}{480} \times 100 = \frac{750 \times 40}{480} = \frac{30000}{480} = 62.5 \text{ L}$$

Step 3: Cost.
$$\text{Cost} = 62.5 \times \$2.10 = \$131.25$$
